Existing route-interception pattern (page.route(...).abort('failed')) for simulating /api/reagent-sites failure — the direct model for the new error-state @visual test the spec requires.

The view under test. onMounted currently rethrows on fetch failure with no visible error UI rendered (just an unhandled pageerror) — the analyst must decide whether an error-state element needs to be added before it can be screenshotted, since none exists today.
Defines the nav link (data-testid="reagent-map-link", lines 12-17) that the page-header screenshot AC covers, including its v-if on the feature flag.

Must gain snapshotPathTemplate and the RUNNER_VARIANT-driven per-image baseline directory; already shows the existing 'chrome' project and resolveRunnerSlowMo()/resolveRunnerVideo() pattern for reading env vars at call time, which the new RUNNER_VARIANT skip logic should match.
Needs a new --update-baselines flag (and --ubi9 composability) plus RUNNER_VARIANT export into the container; shows the existing parse_args/exit-code contract this must extend.
Existing stubbed-docker test harness pattern the spec requires be extended to cover the new --update-baselines flag; shows the fake_docker dispatch style to follow.
Contains the 'No visual baselines' Known Gaps entry (around line 309) the spec requires be closed, and the existing writing-style-governed doc structure to extend.
Must document when to regenerate baselines (including after a browser lock bump) alongside the existing 'Updating the browsers (both locks)' section it should cross-reference.

Direct precedent from the prior feature in this same bounded context: its Recommendations section already concluded the Cesium canvas is a poor pixel-diff target and that screenshotting the DOM-level chrome (site list, nav link, loading/error states) around it is more stable — exactly the approach this spec's ACs take.
